title: Review: Introduction to the particulate nature of matter; The nuclear atom
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for IB Diploma Chemistry (status of the source: ai-reviewed-reverified-gate-verified-2026-09-30-awaiting-human-signoff). Terms and clues: S1.2#c01 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; S1.1#c03 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; S1.2#c05 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; S1.2#c10 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: S1.1#q12, S1.2#q04, S1.2#q10, S1.2#q05, S1.2#q14, S1.1#q08, S1.1#q10, S1.1#q14, S1.2#q01, S1.2#q07, S1.1#q06, S1.1#q11. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Nucleus
items.clue: The small, dense, positively charged centre of an atom, made of protons and neutrons.

items.label: Mixture
items.clue: Two or more elements or compounds that are present together in no fixed ratio and are not chemically bonded to each other.

items.label: Electron
items.clue: A particle with relative charge −1 and relative mass about 0.0005 (about 1/1836 of the mass of a proton), so its mass can be considered negligible.

items.label: Isotopes
items.clue: Atoms of the same element (same atomic number, so the same number of protons) with different numbers of neutrons, and therefore different mass numbers.

questions.stem: On a cold, clear night, water vapour in the air turns directly into ice crystals on a car windscreen, without first becoming liquid water. What is the name of this change of state?

options.text: Condensation
Freezing
Deposition
Sublimation

questions.explanation: A direct change from gas to solid, H₂O(g) → H₂O(s), is deposition. It is the reverse of sublimation.

questions.stem: How many electrons are there in one ³³₁₆S²⁻ ion (mass number 33, atomic number 16, charge 2−)?
questions.explanation: Correct. Z = 16, so there are 16 protons. A charge of 2− means two more electrons than protons: 16 + 2 = 18 electrons. (The ion has 33 − 16 = 17 neutrons.)

questions.stem: Copper has two isotopes, copper-63 and copper-65, with relative isotopic masses 62.93 and 64.93. The relative atomic mass of copper is 63.55. What is the percentage abundance of copper-65?
questions.explanation: Correct. Let x% be copper-65: 64.93x + 62.93(100 − x) = 6355, so 2.00x = 62, x = 31.0. A check: A_r (63.55) is closer to 62.93, so copper-63 should be the more abundant isotope, as it is (69.0%).

questions.stem: An ion X³⁺ contains 23 electrons and 30 neutrons. Which nuclear symbol represents this ion? (Each symbol is written with its superscript first and its subscript second.)

options.text: ⁵⁰₂₀X³⁺
⁵³₂₃X³⁺
⁵⁶₂₆X³⁺
²⁶₅₆X³⁺

questions.explanation: Correct. A 3+ ion has three fewer electrons than protons, so protons = 23 + 3 = 26 = Z. Mass number A = protons + neutrons = 26 + 30 = 56.

questions.stem: How many neutrons are there in one atom of ⁸¹₃₅Br (mass number 81, atomic number 35)?
questions.explanation: Correct. The mass number 81 counts the protons and neutrons; the atomic number 35 is the number of protons. Neutrons = A − Z = 81 − 35 = 46.

questions.stem: A student wants to recover all of the potassium chloride, as a solid, from a dilute aqueous solution of potassium chloride. Which method should be used?

options.text: Filtration, as the dissolved solid is held back on the paper
Cooling, as the dissolved solid freezes when cold enough
Evaporation, as the water escapes and the solid is left behind
Decanting, as the dissolved solid settles to the bottom on standing

questions.explanation: Heating the solution in an open dish vaporizes the water, which escapes into the air; potassium chloride does not vaporize, so the solid is left in the dish. Evaporation recovers the solute; distillation would be used to collect the water.

questions.stem: Which statement about the vaporization of water is correct?

options.text: Evaporation can take place only once the water has reached its boiling point
Evaporation takes place at the surface, even well below the boiling point
The large bubbles in boiling water contain hydrogen and oxygen
The large bubbles in boiling water are air from the gaps between the particles

questions.explanation: Water particles have a range of kinetic energies. At any temperature some particles at the surface have enough energy to overcome the attractions and escape, which is why puddles dry at 20 °C. Boiling, with bubbles of vapour throughout the liquid, happens at the boiling point.

questions.stem: A sample of neon gas is at 77 °C. It is heated until the average kinetic energy of its atoms has doubled. What is its new temperature? (T/K = T/°C + 273)
questions.explanation: Average kinetic energy is proportional to temperature in kelvin. 77 °C = 350 K; doubling gives 700 K; 700 − 273 = 427 °C.

questions.stem: Which statement about the nucleus of an atom is correct?

options.text: It takes up most of the atom's volume, with electrons at its surface.
Its density is far greater than the average density of the atom.
It contains only about two-thirds of the mass of the atom.
It contains the electrons as well as the protons and neutrons.

questions.explanation: Correct. Nearly all of the atom's mass is in the nucleus, because electrons are so light. The nucleus is of order 10⁻¹⁵ m across and the atom of order 10⁻¹⁰ m, so the nucleus occupies only about (10⁻¹⁵ ÷ 10⁻¹⁰)³ = 10⁻¹⁵ of the atom's volume. Nearly all the mass in a tiny volume makes the nucleus extremely dense.

questions.stem: Chlorine (atomic number 17) has isotopes with mass numbers 35 and 37. Pure samples of ³⁵Cl₂ gas and ³⁷Cl₂ gas are compared at the same temperature and pressure. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The ³⁷Cl₂ gas diffuses more slowly than ³⁵Cl₂.
The two gases diffuse at the same rate as each other.
The two gases undergo different chemical reactions.
The ³⁷Cl₂ molecules contain more electrons than ³⁵Cl₂.

questions.explanation: Correct. At the same temperature the molecules of both gases have the same mean kinetic energy, so the heavier ³⁷Cl₂ molecules move more slowly on average and the gas diffuses more slowly. Rate of diffusion is a physical property that differs between isotopes.

questions.stem: A spot of black ink is placed on the baseline of a strip of chromatography paper, and the bottom of the paper is dipped in water. As the water rises, the ink separates into three coloured spots at different heights. What does this show about the ink?

options.text: It is a mixture of several different dyes
It is a mixture of several different elements
It is a compound the paper has separated out
It is a single dye that has reacted with water

questions.explanation: More than one spot shows more than one component. Each dye is carried a different distance up the paper, according to how strongly it is attracted to the paper compared with the water. The dyes were already present and are unchanged.

questions.stem: Which change of state is correctly named and correctly represented by an equation with state symbols?

options.text: Melting: NaCl(s) → NaCl(aq)
Condensation: H₂O(g) → H₂O(s)
Boiling: H₂O(aq) → H₂O(g)
Sublimation: CO₂(s) → CO₂(g)

questions.explanation: At atmospheric pressure solid carbon dioxide ('dry ice') changes directly into gas without becoming liquid. A direct change from solid to gas is sublimation, and the state symbols (s) and (g) show exactly that.
